title: Eternal Inflation and the Measure Problem
bottleneck: Most inflationary potentials lead to eternal inflation, spawning infinite pocket universes — but probabilities over an infinite multiverse are undefined without a 'measure,' and every proposed measure gives different predictions or paradoxes (youngness, Boltzmann brains). There is no consensus on how to extract testable predictions from eternal inflation. Proposals like the scale-factor cutoff, causal patch, and watcher measures each suffer paradoxes or ambiguities that have resisted decades of effort.
why_it_blocks: Without a measure, inflation's most generic prediction — a multiverse — yields no falsifiable numbers, straining its scientific status.
current_state: The measure problem is as open as ever; it is widely considered the deepest obstacle to making multiverse cosmology predictive. Many cosmologists now treat the measure problem as a reason to doubt eternal inflation itself rather than a puzzle to solve.
